data.name: After All
data.detailed_description:
Once upon a time, an evil Demon Lord ruled the world. Your whole life has been spent training for the moment you and your companions could defeat the Demon Lord and save the world. Wielding incredible power, your victory is almost certain. However, after Good triumphs, what happens to you and your young friends? The rest of the land will hail you as heroes, certainly, but what happens with youth who have that much power? Will you grow depressed with the lack of challenge life presents? Will you bask in the adulation of the public but become lazy and gluttonous? Will you enslave the weak and become the next Demon Lord? Or will friendship, love, and all that sappy nonsense nevertheless save the day again?

Find out in this unique RPG that explores common RPG types and what might be after the end of their childhood adventures.

reviews.review:
After All is a narrative-driven RPG developed by JAMgames and published by W. T. B. that takes an uncommon approach to fantasy storytelling. Instead of chronicling a hero's rise to greatness or their final confrontation with an ancient evil, the game begins once those events have already passed. The world has been saved, the celebrations are over, and the heroes who once stood at the center of history are left to figure out what comes next. It is a simple premise, but one that immediately sets the title apart from countless role-playing games that follow a more familiar formula.

The game's greatest strength lies in its willingness to explore life beyond the traditional ending. Players spend their time learning how former adventurers cope with ordinary existence after years of living with purpose and danger. This gives the story a reflective quality that feels surprisingly mature. Themes of identity, friendship, and finding meaning after achieving one's greatest accomplishment are woven throughout the experience. There is an undeniable charm in seeing characters struggle with everyday concerns after spending years battling threats that once determined the fate of the world. While the writing does not always reach the emotional heights it aims for, it frequently succeeds in creating moments that feel sincere and relatable.

Presentation-wise, After All is unmistakably a product of RPG Maker. Its visual style relies on familiar pixel-art assets and straightforward environments that prioritize function over spectacle. Towns, interiors, and surrounding areas are competently designed, even if they lack a distinctive artistic signature. The soundtrack complements the quieter tone of the game, emphasizing introspection rather than adventure. Together, the visuals and music create an atmosphere that feels nostalgic, almost as if players are revisiting a world they once knew well. Fans of indie RPGs may appreciate this simplicity, though others may wish for more visual variety and polish.

Gameplay takes a backseat to the narrative, which can be both a positive and a negative depending on expectations. Exploration and conversations form the core of the experience, with mechanics remaining relatively uncomplicated throughout. Those looking for strategic combat systems, extensive progression mechanics, or lengthy quests may find the game somewhat lacking. Instead, After All focuses on delivering a compact and personal story. Its pacing occasionally falters, particularly during slower stretches where dialogue outweighs meaningful interaction, but the game's commitment to its central concept keeps it engaging enough to encourage players to see the journey through to its conclusion.

At times, the title feels constrained by its limited scope and resources. Certain ideas are introduced without receiving the depth they deserve, leaving players wanting a more expansive look at the lives of its characters and the world they inhabit. Technical limitations and rough edges are also apparent, reminding players that this is a small independent production. However, these shortcomings are easier to forgive when viewed alongside the game's ambition. Few RPGs attempt to tell a story about what happens after the adventure ends, and fewer still make that idea the centerpiece of the entire experience.

After All may not appeal to everyone, particularly players seeking action-packed encounters or groundbreaking mechanics, but it offers a thoughtful alternative to the genre's usual conventions. It succeeds most when it asks players to consider the cost of heroism and the challenge of moving forward once a lifelong purpose has been fulfilled. Although its execution is uneven and its production values are modest, its originality and heartfelt storytelling leave a lasting impression. For players willing to embrace a slower and more contemplative RPG, After All provides a memorable journey that proves there can still be meaningful stories left to tell long after the final battle has been won.

Rating: 5/10
